events.content: STRATEGY: EXPLAIN_NEED — I should say why I cook most nights and propose a simple, fair set of rules so I'm not singled out. Options: defend, propose rules, or concede. Chosen: explain need briefly, state I'm willing to cooperate, and offer concrete steps (rinse/load pans, use extractor/open window, pick no-cook nights or rotate). Keep tone calm and direct; avoid embarrassing anyone.

Look—I cook most nights because I work from home and it's my break, and I also buy the dish soap and gas. I get the smell and the dirty pan are annoying, but please don't single me out in front of everyone. Let's keep cooking but set simple rules: everyone rinses and either washes or puts used pans in the rack the same night, and we open the window and use the extractor. If someone wants quiet weeknights, say which nights and we can rotate or agree no-cook nights.
Waiting to see what Jamie, Casey, and Robin say.

Okay, fair. Alex, can you open the window, turn the extractor on and put the pan in the rack now? I start early and need to sleep.

scenario.shared_setting: Four adults have shared a rented HDB flat for eight months. There is one kitchen with one stove, a window, and a working extractor fan, and all four people cook there. The household has never agreed any rules about the kitchen. It is a weeknight evening and all four are in the kitchen and the living area next to it. All four will be living here and using this kitchen again tomorrow, and for the rest of the lease.
